cases.answer: In the Hunan retrospective neoadjuvant NSCLC cohort (clinical stage IB–IIIB), the unadjusted MPR rate was 49.3% (34/69) with PD-1 inhibitor plus chemotherapy, versus 19.0% (23/121) with chemotherapy alone (p < 0.001). After propensity-score matching the rates were 48.4% vs 17.2% (p = 0.001), but those are the adjusted figures.

cases.answer: The two figures are not directly comparable. Helsinki (single-centre, retrospective, 75 TNBC patients given neoadjuvant chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab) reports an absolute frequency: 11 patients (14.7%) had grade 1–2 myocarditis. The lung-cancer RCT meta-analysis (Yamani et al.) reports relative risks versus a control arm, not absolute frequencies. Single ICI had RR 2.15 (95% CI 1.13–4.12) and single ICI plus chemotherapy had RR 1.38 (95% CI 1.05–1.82) for any cardiac adverse event versus chemotherapy. For myocarditis specifically, the pooled RR for ICI versus control was 1.67 (95% CI 0.67–4.16, p = 0.27), which is not significant. The populations (TNBC vs lung cancer), designs (uncontrolled cohort vs pooled RCTs) and outcome definitions all differ. The Helsinki authors note their rate exceeds that of KEYNOTE-522 (0.4%) and attribute this partly to differences in grading guidelines.

cases.answer: In reflex testing the pathologist handling the case initiates and controls testing for a set of prespecified biomarkers. The MDT agrees that biomarker set (the protocol) beforehand. No formal request from an oncologist is required. The reported delay mechanism is in the traditional oncologist-led pathway. Tests are ordered by the treating oncologist only after a pathological diagnosis is confirmed, which adds a step before testing starts. This prolongs the pre-treatment pathway and delays first-line systemic treatment. Reflex testing instead begins as soon as the diagnosis is confirmed, rather than after the first post-biopsy oncology appointment or MDT discussion. Long turnaround times can also deter clinicians from ordering tests, and delayed reporting risks clinical deterioration and starting suboptimal therapy before biomarker status is complete.

cases.answer: The two articles address different questions and do not link directly. The Hunan study (retrospective, clinical stage IB–IIIB NSCLC, December 2018–December 2020) contributes treatment-efficacy evidence. Neoadjuvant PD-1 plus chemotherapy (69 patients) gave a higher MPR rate than chemotherapy alone (121 patients), 49.3% vs 19.0% (p < 0.001). It also gave better 2-year DFS (79.3% vs 60.2%, p = 0.048), and pathological response was an independent prognostic factor for DFS. It reports no biomarker data, and I found no PD-L1, EGFR or driver-gene testing in it. The Gosney consensus contributes the testing-process side. It argues that biomarker results should be available early through pathologist-initiated reflex testing under an MDT-agreed, stage-agnostic protocol. It says this is now also vital in early-stage resectable disease, because adjuvant targeted therapy (ADAURA) is established and targeted therapies are becoming established in the neoadjuvant setting. Together, the Hunan results show the benefit of the chemoimmunotherapy strategy. The consensus indicates that complete biomarker status should be known before perioperative treatment is chosen. Neither article shows how biomarker status related to response in the Hunan patients, so no such link can be drawn.

cases.answer: The review (Tiwari et al.) distinguishes the three phenotypes by where lymphocytes sit relative to the tumor parenchyma and stroma. Inflamed (hot) tumors have lymphocytic infiltration in the tumor parenchyma, with immune cells close to tumor cells. Desert (cold) tumors lack lymphocytes in the parenchyma or the periphery, although the term has often been used for tumors that merely lack lymphocytes in the center, ignoring the periphery. Excluded tumors have abundant immune cells in the TME, but these are confined to the stroma and do not penetrate the tumor parenchyma. The review notes that definitions across the literature are inconsistent and largely conceptual.

tumor parenchyma, with the immune cells positioned in proximity to
